projectSummary: This trial supports two distinct statements: that eight weeks of bench-press-only training changes pectoralis major thickness in untrained men, and that the change is not uniform across measurement sites. It cannot speak to a cable fly, and its once-weekly frequency is unusually low.

publication.statusSource: Crossref REST API works record plus the Crossref/Retraction Watch CSV export, both fetched 2026-09-13

notes: Only 30 of 47 randomised participants contributed muscle thickness data, and the report does not state why the remaining 17 did not.
Once-weekly training is at the low end of prescribed frequencies and limits generalisation.
Site labels are intercostal spaces on the rib cage, not clavicular and sternocostal heads, so the regional statement is site-specific rather than portion-specific.
There is no non-training control arm, so the within-group change cannot be separated from time, familiarisation and measurement drift.

study.intervention: horizontal bench press; incline bench press; combination
study.population: Forty-seven untrained men were randomly assigned to a horizontal bench press group (n = 15), an incline bench press group (n = 15), or a combination group (n = 17). Training was once per week for eight weeks with the number of sets equalised across groups.

title: Effects of Horizontal and Incline Bench Press on Neuromuscular Adaptations in Untrained Young Men.
